bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42473363 (gnutls): Heap-use-after-free READ 8 found by fuzz target gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42473363
bug_description.normalized: The staged 3349-byte DER witness is accepted by `gnutls_pkcs12_import`, and `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` reaches its second pass because the first pass successfully imports at least one private-key bag and sets `privkey_ok = 1`. In that second pass, a bag element of type `GNUTLS_BAG_CRL` exposes attacker-controlled CRL bytes, `gnutls_x509_crl_init` allocates a heap CRL object into the caller-owned output slot `*crl`, and `gnutls_x509_crl_import(*crl, &data, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER)` then fails on the same witness. The vulnerable error path deinitializes `*crl` at `lib/x509/pkcs12.c:1745` but does not clear the output pointer before `goto done`. Common cleanup later re-tests `if (crl != NULL && *crl != NULL)` and calls `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` again at `lib/x509/pkcs12.c:1791`; inside `lib/x509/crl.c:98`, `if (crl->crl)` reads from the freed object and AddressSanitizer reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8`. The staged fix inserts `*crl = NULL` immediately after the first `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)`, so the common cleanup no longer reuses the dangling alias.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled blob into the internal PKCS#12 structure later walked by `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 3349-byte binary blob beginning `30 82 0d 11 ...`; the fuzz target passes it to `gnutls_pkcs12_import(p12, &raw, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, 0)`, and the saved run reaches `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`, proving these bytes decode as a PKCS#12 object.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code:
type = gnutls_pkcs12_bag_get_type(bag, i);
ret = gnutls_pkcs12_bag_get_data(bag, i, &data);
tainted_value_origin.description: In the second pass, the parser materializes the current bag element's kind and payload. For the crashing witness, this step exposes the CRL bag bytes in `data`, and those bytes drive the failing `gnutls_x509_crl_import` call.

root_cause.description: On CRL import failure, the error branch frees the newly allocated CRL object but leaves the caller-owned output pointer non-NULL before jumping to common cleanup. That stale alias is what the later cleanup reuses.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `*crl = NULL` immediately after this call before `goto done`, preventing the second cleanup from re-entering `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit` on freed storage.

sink.description: ASan sink. During the second `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl)` call, this field read dereferences the already freed CRL object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports the crashing 8-byte read at `lib/x509/crl.c:98`, with the earlier free attributed to `lib/x509/pkcs12.c:1745` and the allocating call to `lib/x509/crl.c:73`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted as DER-encoded PKCS#12 and populates `p12->pkcs12`; otherwise the saved run would not reach `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`.

private_key_found.description: The second pass only runs after the first pass successfully imports a private key bag and sets `privkey_ok`, avoiding the `privkey_ok == 0` early return at line 1593.

fine_trace.note: Parses the attacker-controlled DER blob into `pkcs12->pkcs12`, creating the internal PKCS#12 structure that later bag walks consume.

This assignment occurs only after `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8(...)` and `gnutls_x509_privkey_get_key_id(...)` succeed on a key bag, so the function does not take the `privkey_ok == 0` return and proceeds to the second parsing pass.

fine_trace.code:
type = gnutls_pkcs12_bag_get_type(bag, i);
ret = gnutls_pkcs12_bag_get_data(bag, i, &data);
fine_trace.note: In the second pass, one bag element resolves to `GNUTLS_BAG_CRL`, and its attacker-controlled payload is materialized in `data` for the CRL branch.
Because this element is handled by `case GNUTLS_BAG_CRL` and `*crl` is still NULL, the code allocates a fresh heap CRL object and stores its address in the caller-owned output slot `*crl`.
The same CRL bag payload is imported into the freshly allocated object, and on the staged witness this call returns a negative error.
On the import-failure path, the code frees the CRL object but leaves `*crl` unchanged before `goto done`, so the caller-owned output slot becomes a dangling non-NULL alias.
Shared error cleanup re-tests the stale output slot and decides that CRL cleanup should run again because the dangling pointer still compares non-NULL.
The common cleanup invokes CRL deinit a second time on the dangling pointer.
Inside the second deinit call, the first field access dereferences the freed CRL object. AddressSanitizer reports the crashing 8-byte heap-use-after-free read here.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not preserve which exact PKCS#12 bag index supplied the successful private key or the failing CRL, nor whether the key bag was plain or encrypted. The source-grounded facts needed for closure are narrower: the first pass set `privkey_ok = 1`, the second pass reached `GNUTLS_BAG_CRL`, `gnutls_x509_crl_import` failed, and `*crl` was freed without being cleared before common cleanup reused it.

allocation_context.description: ASan attributes the later invalid read address to the `gnutls_calloc(1, sizeof(gnutls_x509_crl_int))` allocation that `gnutls_x509_crl_init` stores into `*crl`.

free_context.description: The first free comes from the import-failure cleanup call `gnutls_x509_crl_deinit(*crl);` inside `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse`.

format.name: DER PKCS#12
format.contract: The staged `poc` is a DER-encoded PKCS#12 blob accepted by `gnutls_pkcs12_import`; under the harness's fixed password `1234`, `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` must find at least one private-key bag so `privkey_ok` becomes 1, then later encounter a CRL bag whose payload makes `gnutls_x509_crl_import(*crl, &data, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER)` fail after `gnutls_x509_crl_init` has already stored a heap CRL object in `*crl`.
